sections.content:
Population change in Harrow in 2032

The population in Harrow is projected to increase from 261,933 people in 2022 to 274,599 people in 2032.

Despite an overall increase in the population, there is projected to be a fall in net internal migration, which will decrease the population by 38,202 people.

This will also be the biggest factor in population change in most areas in England.

sections.title: Contributors to population change in Harrow
sections.subtitle: How the population is projected to change, by cause
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant
sections.note: The components of change do not always sum exactly to the total population change in an area. This is primarily due to the effect of constraining the final projections to the National Population Projections for England.

sections.content:
Population change is projected by looking at births and deaths (natural change) and people moving in and out of areas. In Harrow, our projections show that between 2022 and 2032:

  • More births than deaths mean that the population is projected to increase by 13,958, with 31,634 births and 17,677 deaths in Harrow between 2022 and 2032. This means natural change would increase the population in Harrow by 5.3%, compared with an increase of 6.0% in London and an increase of 0.2% in England.
  • Net internal migration (people moving to and from other local authorities in England) is projected to reduce the population by 38,202, with 189,042 people moving to the area and 227,244 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Harrow by 14.6%.
  • Net cross-border migration (between UK nations) is projected to reduce the population by 987, with 2,990 people moving to the area and 3,977 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would decrease the population in Harrow by 0.4%.
  • Net international migration is projected to increase the population by 37,822, with 73,011 people moving to the area and 35,189 people moving from the area between 2022 and 2032. This would increase the population in Harrow by 14.4%, compared with an increase of 14.7% in London and an increase of 6.5% in England.

sections.content:
Age profile in Harrow in 2032

The median age in Harrow is projected to rise from 38 years in 2022 to 39 years in 2032.

In England, the median age is projected to be 41 years in 2032.

In 2032, 17% of the population in Harrow are projected to be aged 65 years or over, up from 15% in 2022.

sections.title: The 0 to 9 age group are set to see the largest change in Harrow between 2022 and 2032
sections.subtitle: Percentages of population by 10 year age bands, 2022 and 2032
sections.source: Subnational population projections for England from Office for National Statistics – Migration category variant

sections.content:
Between 2022 and 2032, the share of the working age population (people aged 16 years to State Pension age) in Harrow is projected to stay the same, at around 65%.

The old age dependency ratio (the number of people of State Pension age for every 1,000 people of working age) is projected to rise from 226 to 238 over the same time period.

This is below average for England in 2032 (287 per 1,000). Nationally, a high old age dependency ratio means more older people are financially reliant on the working age population to pay for pensions.

How will the number of young people change in Harrow?

In 2032, 22% of people are projected to be aged 18 years and under, down from 24% in 2022.

This is above average for England in 2032 (20%).

Looking at the youngest age groups in Harrow between 2022 and 2032, we can see the share of:

  • Infants (aged 0 to 4 years) will stay around the same, at 6%
  • Primary school age children (aged 5 to 11 years) will fall from 9% to 8%
  • Secondary school age children and sixth-form age (aged 12 to 18 years) will fall from 9% to 8%
